thread:
Natalie Support: heads up — we're getting a flood of 403s for prod deploys. Root cause looks like the CI runner can't impersonate the service account. Start time ~07:12 UTC. Repro steps below. SUP-4287 created for tracking.

deploy-bot: [automated log] deploy failed: status=403, message=Request had insufficient authentication scopes. Details:
```
ERROR: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor does not have permission to actAs serviceAccount: projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/sa-ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
at runtime/serving: attempt impersonation -> iam.serviceAccounts.actAs denied
```

Ben Infra: can you paste the minimal repro command? also please include the last Identity Token printed by the runner (sanitized ok).

Natalie Support: minimal repro (from a dev VM, failing the same way):
```bash
export CI_SA=sa-ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=${CI_SA} --audiences=https://redwood-inference.internal/deploy || true
# exit code non-zero, prints error about not being allowed to impersonate
```

Omar Ops: hmm. Two likely failure modes: 1) the deploy bot identity doesn't have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA, or 2) IAM Conditions on the SA policy are blocking short-lived impersonation (audience/method mismatch).

Lisa Dev: also check the token lifetime the runner requests. We've had cases where the OIDC provider erroneously requests a 5s TTL for initial handshake and the IAM Condition expects >=30s which fails.

Ben Infra: run this to inspect current bindings quickly:
```bash
gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy ${CI_SA} --project=redwood-prod 
```
Look for members like user:deploy-bot@redwood.com or serviceAccount:gitlab-runner@... and check for `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` or `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`. If missing, that's the immediate cause.

Natalie Support: I ran that and saw only a narrow binding: a group `ci-runners@redwood.com` has roles/iam.serviceAccountUser but no TokenCreator. There is an IAM Condition on the binding requiring request.auth.aud == "https://redwood-inference.internal/deploy". The runners set audience to the GCP default which doesn't match.

Omar Ops: ok this explains it — audience mismatch + missing TokenCreator. Quick triage options:
- Temporary: grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to the deploy-bot (or ci-runners group) on the target SA so impersonation succeeds.
- Safer: fix CI OIDC audience to match the IAM Condition, or relax the condition to include the runner audience.
- Least-privilege path: create a short-lived delegating SA which has only tokenCreator on sa-ci-runner and restrict which subjects can mint tokens via IAM Conditions.

Lisa Dev: here's a minimal terraform snippet to add TokenCreator as a temporary relief (remember to revert after audit):
```hcl
resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "ci_token_creator" {
  project = "redwood-prod"
  service_account_id = "sa-ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  role = "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
  members = ["group:ci-runners@redwood.com"]
}
```

Ben Infra: note: `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` alone won't let you mint tokens — it's for actAs on the SA in some contexts but token minting requires TokenCreator. Also double-check whether the runner uses `impersonate` vs `oauth2` flow.

Natalie Support: I pushed the temporary binding to the `staging-ops` branch and applied to the prod SA for 1 hour — deploys are immediately succeeding again. :thumbsup: Will roll back in 1h and follow the permanent plan.

Omar Ops: good. Next actions for the permanent fix (assign owners):
1) Ben Infra: audit all SAs referenced in CI to ensure TokenCreator bindings exist only where necessary, open follow-up ticket SUP-4287-1.
2) Lisa Dev: update the GitLab/GHA OIDC audience to `https://redwood-inference.internal/deploy` or adjust the IAM Condition to allow both audiences. SUP-4287-2.
3) Natalie Support: add an alert that surfaces `iam:impersonation:denied` in the SLO dashboard when we see >5/min. SUP-4287-3.

Lisa Dev: small note on least privilege: we should avoid giving broad TokenCreator to humans. Prefer: create a CI-specific minimal SA `sa-ci-delegator` with TokenCreator on `sa-ci-runner` and give the runner the ability to impersonate `sa-ci-delegator`. That keeps blast radius small.

Ben Infra: agree. Also add a short-lived TTL guard in our deploy orchestration: fail early if requested token_ttl < 30s. That prevents accidental tiny TTLs caused by OIDC misconfig.

sre-bot: [monitoring] Event: deploy-failure-rate increased -> 403 impersonation errors. Alert suppressed after remediation.

Natalie Support: follow-up notes for support docs (I'll update):
- What happened: CI runner couldn't mint impersonation token because TokenCreator missing and audience didn't match IAM Condition.
- Short-term mitigation: grant roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to ci-runners group for the specific SA (applied and will be rolled back).
- Long-term: adopt delegated SA pattern + audit + TTL guard + update OIDC audience.

Omar Ops: thanks all. Ben/Lisa please DM me once your PRs are up. Marking this thread resolved for now. :eyes:

Natalie Support: resolved (temporary fix applied). Last action: created SUP-4287 with the three follow-ups and linking this thread.
